signature: SUBROUTINE DLASWP( N, A, LDA, K1, K2, IPIV, INCX )

params.name: N
params.reference: The number of columns of the matrix A.

params.name: A
params.reference: On entry, the matrix of column dimension N to which the row interchanges will be applied. On exit, the permuted matrix.

params.name: lda
params.reference: The leading dimension of the array A.

params.name: k1
params.reference: The first element of `IPIV` for which a row interchange will be done.

params.name: k2
params.reference: (`K2`-`K1`+1) is the number of elements of `IPIV` for which a row interchange will be done.

params.name: IPIV
params.reference: The vector of pivot indices. Only the elements in positions `K1` through $K_{1}+(K_{2}-K_{1}) \, \lvert \mathrm{INCX} \rvert$ of `IPIV` are accessed. `IPIV(K1+(K-K1)*abs(INCX)) = L` implies rows K and L are to be interchanged.

params.name: inck
params.reference: The increment between successive values of `IPIV`. If `INCX` is negative, the pivots are applied in reverse order.

overrides.reason: INCX is both IPIV's stride and the pivot direction (its sign selects reverse order). The JS carries the IPIV stride separately as strideIPIV and keeps INCX as a plain direction scalar, so it is not a consumed increment.

stdlib's dlaswp API (lapack/base/dlaswp) takes the direction as `inck` before IPIV: `( N, A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA, k1, k2, inck, IPIV, strideIPIV, offsetIPIV )`; the JS keeps that order and name.
